head: b7ee4555810dcb82b4a0714200c599ab076daac8
summary: Maintainers can authorize an agent to merge an Ask PR with no required checks through a head-specific confirmation. The change adds bounded maintenance and unconditional workflow text; real-use impact and full instruction-growth measurements remain unknown.
reasons: The change directly addresses #551: maintainers can tell the agent to merge an approved Ask PR when neither GitHub nor the trusted seam requires checks.

The confirmation excuses only an empty check set for the submitted head. Existing check, review, base, merge-state, and queue gates remain. User authorization and the Ask restriction remain agent responsibilities, explicitly identified in enforcement.yml.

Maintenance stays bounded to one confirmation flag, result field, setup warning, and focused tests. The warning supports the existing Auto restriction; no new dependency or configuration setting appears.

The added workflow instruction governs a non-obvious authorization decision that Ruby cannot establish. SKILL.md loads the complete rendered workflow for every task, so its approximately 30 added words impose an unconditional reading cost. The packet omits the actual instruction-growth report and byte measurements, limiting cost verification without demonstrating an architectural violation.

Three local review rounds fixed one risk; CodeRabbit findings were also fixed. The remaining reported findings are wording nits. Real-use benefit, incident frequency, and time saved are unknown; the evidence demonstrates the supported path through fake-client tests.
alternative: Keep the GitHub-click workaround if maintainers prefer avoiding another CLI flag; that preserves safeguards but leaves the reported Ask workflow interruption unresolved.
next_action: Attach the existing bin/report-instruction-growth output to the checkpoint evidence to complete the instruction-cost record.
